title: Seller Rescue: Three-Act Playbook for Pilot Breaks (Draft)
content:
Purpose: quick, low-friction playbook sellers can run when a pilot or demo hits an inference reliability or cost surprise. This is intentionally pragmatic and script-first — use the act headings during a 30–45 minute huddle with SE + customer.

Context and when to use:
- Pilot or POC: customers evaluating end-to-end inference (latency/cost/accuracy) and we detect a regress, latency spike, or unexpected spend.
- Demo: live demo fails (timeouts, truncated responses, hallucinations where prior was OK).
- Early production: rollouts where a percentage of traffic hits a new model variant and metrics diverge.

Three-Act structure (why three acts?): concise cognitive framing for sellers — detect, triage, rescue/recover.

ACT I: DETECT (first 5–10 mins)
- Seller check: "Is the customer seeing errors or degraded responses? Are tokens increasing?"
- Signals to watch: 5xx rate >1% above baseline, median p95 latency +30% over last hour, token count per request > expected, QA eval run shows quality delta >5 points.
- Quick probe script (copy/paste to customer or run with SE):
  1) Reproduce the failing prompt (send identical), log request_id.
  2) Check model + route: modelId, modelVariant, region, route policy.
  3) Ask: "Has anything changed on your input side? prompt length? context injection?"
- Immediate seller language: "We see a deviation — running a short probe with our SE to pinpoint root cause, will keep you looped in the next 20 mins"

ACT II: TRIAGE (10–20 mins)
- Owner: SE + on-call pilot engineer (if available).
- Triage checklist (fast):
  - Confirm reproducibility across 3 requests.
  - Compare responses across two model variants (current vs stable pin).
  - Check runtime telemetry: batch size spikes, queue length, GPU mem pressure, KV cache hit rate.
  - Cost heuristic: tokens per minute increased? sudden embedding/recall calls?
- Low-effort mitigation steps (apply in order, stop when fixed):
  1) Switch to stable model variant (if routing allows) for the failing route — scripted rollback command for ops: "route.update --route-id <r> --model stable-v{n}".
  2) Reduce max_tokens and/or set stricter stop sequences for the route to lower tail latency and token spend.
  3) Enable prefix KV cache for repeated context-heavy prompts.
  4) Toggle continuous batching policy to lower allowed batch size during latency-sensitive route.
- Seller script to customer during triage: "We’re trying a quick rollback to a stable variant and tight token controls to confirm whether this is runtime or model quality. This should take ~10 mins and won’t affect your data."

ACT III: RESCUE & RECOVER (20–45 mins)
- If mitigation worked: document timeline, record metrics (latency, errors, token spend), propose follow-up A/B test to validate quality tradeoffs.
- If mitigations fail: escalate to Platform SRE + Applied ML. Use standard escalation template below.
- Recovery checklist:
  - Run a short eval suite (10–20 prompts) comparing pre-incident vs post-mitigation outputs.
  - Capture token economics: pre-incident tokens/min and post-mitigation tokens/min.
  - Recommend permanent action: pin to stable model, adjust batching policy, or schedule a rollout hold for full rollback.

Escalation template (DM / email):
- Subject: Pilot incident — [Customer] — route [route-id] — high p95 latency / quality drop
- Body: "Summary: started <timestamp>. Impact: error rate X%, p95 latency +Y ms, tokens/min +Z. Actions attempted: rollback to stable-v{n}, reduced max_tokens to M, toggled batching policy. Attached: 3 reproductions (request_ids), telemetry links, quick eval outputs. Request: please triage model quantization/compilation logs, or confirm kernel fallback in last deploy. On-call: @platform-sre, @applied-ml. Owner: SE [name]."

Customer-facing quick demo fallback flows (use these in demos so sellers don’t scramble):
- Flow A (latency-sensitive demo): pre-pin a low-latency, lower-context model variant; have a demo script truncated to 2–3 exchanges and pre-warmed KV cache.
- Flow B (accuracy-sensitive demo): pin higher-capacity variant, run offline eval and show side-by-side outputs; keep a fast-fallback variant ready if latency crosses threshold.
- Flow C (cost-sensitive pilot): instrument prefix caching + response compression, set early stop tokens, and expose a clear burn forecast in the demo with worst/baseline estimates.

Example seller one-liners and objection responses (short):
- "We can roll traffic to a pinned stable model in about 10 minutes — that buys us time to diagnose without blocking your test."
- If asked about hallucinations: "We’ll run a focused eval on your prompt set and can lock a model that preserves accuracy while we debug the rollout"
- If asked about cost spikes: "We’ll switch to a capped token plan and provide a short-term quota until we find the per-call root cause."

Operational knobs cheat sheet for SEs (plain language):
- Model pin: forces route to a specific model variant (use when quality regressions seen).
- Max_tokens / stop sequences: short-term knobs to limit extra token spend.
- Batching policy: lower batch_size_limit reduces throughput but can improve latency.
- KV cache: turn on for repeated contexts to reduce work per call.
- Quantization profile: if available, try int8-quant variant for cost relief, but confirm eval (possible minor quality delta).

Playbook play-by-play (example scenario):
- 0:00 Seller notices latency anomaly during a live pilot.
- 0:02 Run ACT I probe, get 3 reproducible failing requests.
- 0:07 SE runs ACT II checklist, toggles model pin to stable, reduces max_tokens by 25%.
- 0:12 Customer confirms responses recovered. SE records metrics and schedules a 1-hour follow-up to run the 20-prompt eval.

Post-mortem template items (short bullets):
- Incident start, detection mechanism, root cause (if known), mitigation timeline, metrics (p50/p95 latency, errors, token spend), permanent action, owners, and notes for product (e.g., add route-level auto-fallback to stable by default?).

Quick TODOs for this doc (notes to self):

- Pull sample telemetry links from demo account and attach.
- Run tabletop with 3 SEs + 1 SRE next week to rehearse.
- Convert to a 1-slide cheat sheet and a 3-card battlecard for field kits.

Loose brainstorm / ideas (future):
- Auto-playbook: an API endpoint that runs a verified rollback + token cap sequence automatically for pilot routes that meet threshold.
- Seller-local runbook card: laminated 3-step rescue card for in-person demos.
- Small simulator that shows cost/latency trade-offs by toggling batching/quantization in realtime.

Notes: intentionally terse. Keep this doc close to SE inbox for fast edits.

End.
